html:
A Pakistani television and online music series, running since 2008, in which artists record live in the studio, blending folk, Sufi devotional music, classical and pop.

It was part of a Coca-Cola franchise that began in Brazil, but the Pakistani version, first produced by the musician Rohail Hyatt, gave it its own character. It paired famous pop and rock stars with folk singers, qawwali performers and players of regional instruments, and set old poetry, by Sufi poets such as Bulleh Shah, to new arrangements. Singers such as Abida Parveen, Atif Aslam and Ali Zafar appeared over the years.

It came at a hard time for Pakistan, when militant violence had shut down many concerts. The show became one of the country's most popular cultural exports, watched widely in India and across the South Asian diaspora, despite political tension. In 2022 the song "Pasoori", sung by Ali Sethi and Shae Gill, became a global hit, among the most streamed songs ever from Pakistan. It carries on the Sufi musical tradition in a modern form.
sum: A Pakistani television and online music series, running since 2008, in which artists record live in the studio, blending folk, Sufi devotional music, classical and pop.
